questions.question: What does BLEU measure?
options: Language identification accuracy — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
N-gram precision (typically 1-4) between hypothesis and reference, with a brevity penalty
Character-level F-score
Embedding cosine similarity
questions.explanation: BLEU is the geometric mean of 1-4-gram precision against references, plus a brevity penalty.

questions.question: Why use sacrebleu instead of rolling your own BLEU?
options: It is more accurate
It runs on GPU
It normalizes tokenization so scores are comparable across papers and runs
It supports streaming, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: sacrebleu freezes tokenization, removing a common source of incomparable BLEU numbers.

questions.question: Which NLLB-specific setting controls the target language during decoding?
options: length_penalty, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
forced_bos_token_id set to the target language code's token id
num_beams
src_lang
questions.explanation: NLLB forces the first decoded token to a target-language code via forced_bos_token_id.

questions.question: Which metric family is the 2026 default for production MT quality where labeled data exists?
options: BLEU alone
Token edit distance, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Learned metrics such as COMET (and BERTScore/BLEURT) trained on human judgment
Latency
questions.explanation: Learned metrics like COMET correlate more strongly with human judgment than BLEU/chrF alone.

questions.question: When does chrF tend to be more informative than BLEU?
options: For morphologically rich languages where character-level matches catch inflectional variants BLEU misses
When using beam search
On very short sentences
Whenever a reference exists — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: Character F-score captures partial morphological matches that word-level BLEU undercounts.

questions.question: What is off-target generation in multilingual MT?
options: Output that drops named entities, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
Output that misses punctuation
The model decodes into the wrong target language (e.g. NLLB outputting Spanish when French was requested)
Output that is too short
questions.explanation: Off-target generation is common on rare language pairs; a post-translation language-ID check catches it.
